status_summary: Law-firm reports date the removals of NLRB General Counsel Jennifer Abruzzo and EEOC General Counsel Karla Gilbride to 2025-01-27, along with NLRB Board member Gwynne Wilcox and EEOC commissioners Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels, whose terms had not expired. The NLRB's list shows acting general counsels from 2025-01-28 and Crystal Carey sworn in as General Counsel on 2026-01-07, while the EEOC's list shows Andrew Rogers acting from January to October 2025 and Catherine Eschbach acting from October 2025 to September 2026 (month-only dates) with no successor named, and Bloomberg Government reported on 2026-04-28 that the November 2025 nomination of Carter Crow had been withdrawn, so the EEOC has had no permanent general counsel. On 2026-06-29 the Supreme Court held in Trump v. Slaughter that the FTC commissioners' for-cause removal protection is unconstitutional, without deciding the NLRB or EEOC. In the Wilcox challenge, a D.C. Circuit panel held on 2025-12-05 that the President may remove NLRB members, rehearing en banc was denied on 2026-01-28, and the Supreme Court denied certiorari on 2026-10-19 (No. 26-5).

timeline.event: President Trump removes NLRB General Counsel Jennifer Abruzzo and Board member Gwynne Wilcox, and EEOC General Counsel Karla Gilbride and Commissioners Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels. A law firm client alert reports that the removals left both agencies without a quorum and that the EEOC commissioners' terms ran to July 2028 and July 2026.

William Cowen becomes NLRB Acting General Counsel, replacing Jessica Rutter, who had been acting since 2025-01-28, per the NLRB's list of general counsels; a law-firm report dates the President's designation of Cowen 2025-02-03.
President Trump names Andrew Rogers, who had been chief counsel to then-Acting Chair Andrea Lucas, as EEOC Acting General Counsel.

Catherine Eschbach began serving as EEOC Acting General Counsel in October 2025 (month-only date), succeeding Andrew Rogers, who had been acting since January 2025, per the EEOC's list of its general counsels.

President Trump nominates M. Carter Crow, a Norton Rose Fulbright labor and employment partner, as EEOC General Counsel; a trade report dated 2025-11-19 says Catherine Eschbach was then acting general counsel and that Rogers had left to become Wage and Hour Division Administrator. No Senate action was found.

A D.C. Circuit panel (opinion by Judge Katsas) reverses the district court in Wilcox v. Trump (No. 25-5057), holding that Congress cannot restrict the President's power to remove NLRB members because the Board exercises substantial executive power outside the Humphrey's Executor exception; the decision date is confirmed on the Supreme Court docket for No. 26-5 and the holding rests on a litigation clearinghouse summary.
Crystal Carey is sworn in as NLRB General Counsel, per the NLRB's General Counsel page (the page gives the swearing-in date but not the confirmation date).
The D.C. Circuit denies rehearing en banc in Wilcox v. Trump (No. 25-5057), per the Supreme Court docket for No. 26-5 and a litigation clearinghouse summary.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States (docket)

timeline.event: The White House sends the Senate a notice withdrawing the nomination of Carter Crow as EEOC general counsel, per a Bloomberg Government report dated 2026-04-28 that places the notice on the preceding Monday (date inferred from that wording); the EEOC has had no permanent general counsel since January 2025.

In Trump v. Slaughter (decided 2026-06-29; Roberts, C.J., for the Court, 6-3) the Supreme Court holds that the FTC's for-cause removal protection violates the separation of powers and that the President may remove FTC commissioners, and overrules Humphrey's Executor to the extent anything remains of it. Part III-B (slip op. 27 to 28) reserves the Federal Reserve, non-Article III courts and bodies without executive power; the NLRB appears only in a citation (slip op. 23). The case is reversed and remanded.
Catherine Eschbach's service as EEOC Acting General Counsel ended in September 2026 (month-only date), per the EEOC's list of its general counsels, which names no successor.

The Supreme Court denies the petition for certiorari in Wilcox v. Trump (No. 26-5, filed 2026-06-27; the government first waived a response, the Court requested one on 2026-08-13 and the brief in opposition was filed 2026-09-14), leaving in place the D.C. Circuit judgment that the removal of NLRB member Wilcox was lawful; the case appears under certiorari denied in the order list of the same date.
